title: BVA Decision 25000004: Entitlement to an earlier effective date of November 10, 2003, for the claim of service connection for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is granted
text:
Citation Nr: 25000004
Decision Date: 01/02/25	Archive Date: 01/02/25

DOCKET NO. 17-16 766
DATE: January 2, 2025

ORDER

Entitlement to an earlier effective date of November 10, 2003, for the claim of service connection for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is granted.

FINDING OF FACT

On November 10, 2003 the Veteran submitted a claim for service connection for PTSD that was not finally adjudicated until January 5, 2015, which the Veteran timely appealed.

CONCLUSION OF LAW

The criteria for an earlier effective date of November 10, 2003, for the grant of service connection for PTSD, have been met. 38 U.S.C. § 5100; 38 C.F.R. § 3.400.

REASONS AND BASES FOR FINDING AND CONCLUSION

The Veteran served honorably on active duty in the United States Navy from May 1988 to July 1989.

This matter is before the Board of Veterans' Appeals (Board) on appeal from an April 2016 rating decision issued by the Department of Veterans Affairs agency of original jurisdiction (AOJ). 

In April 2020, the Veteran testified at a Travel Board hearing before a Veterans Law Judge who is no longer at the Board. The AOJ notified the Veteran of the opportunity for another hearing, for which no response was received. A transcript of the hearing is associated with the claims file.

The Veteran appealed the Board's July 30, 2020 decision to the Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims (CAVC). In May 2024, CAVC issued a memorandum decision. In relevant part, the CAVC decision found remand of the Veteran's claim was warranted because the Board failed to provide an adequate statement of reasons and bases regarding whether the Veteran was properly notified of his right to appeal the July 27, 2004 VA administrative decision and whether a July 24, 2006 VA treatment report should have been construed as an informal claim for benefits under the regulations in effect at the time.

This appeal has been advanced on the Board's docket pursuant to 38 C.F.R. § 20.902(c).

Entitlement to an earlier effective date, of November 10, 2003, for the claim of service connection for PTSD.

The Veteran seeks an earlier effective date for the grant of service connection for PTSD. See November 2016 Notice of Disagreement. He seeks the date of November 10, 2003, which is the date he filed his initial claim for PTSD.

The effective date of an award of compensation shall be fixed in accordance with the facts found but shall not be earlier than the date of receipt of application therefor. 38 U.S.C. § 5110(a). The effective date of an award of compensation based on a claim reopened after a final disallowance will be the date of receipt of the claim to reopen, or the date entitlement arose, whichever is later. 38 C.F.R. § 3.400(q)(2), (r).

Regulations governing what constitutes a claim were revised effective March 24, 2015. As the Veteran's claim was received prior to that date, the Board must apply the older regulations. Prior to March 24, 2015, a claim was "a formal or informal communication in writing requesting a determination of entitlement, or evidencing a belief in entitlement, to a benefit." 38 C.F.R. § 3.1(p). An informal claim was "[a]ny communication or action indicating intent to apply for one or more benefits." 38 C.F.R. § 3.155(a).

The currently assigned effective date of December 21, 2009 is based on the date the Veteran filed a VA Form 21-526EZ claim for service connection for PTSD. See January 2015 rating decision. The AOJ had previously denied the Veteran's November 2003 claim in a July 27, 2004 letter notifying the Veteran that a July 14, 2004 administrative decision documented the Veteran's character of discharge was a bar to receiving VA benefits. See July 27, 2004 AOJ correspondence. 

Although the AOJ next provided a statement of the case on the issue of whether the Veteran's character of discharge constituted a bar to VA benefits in May 2011, and a supplemental statement of the case on that matter in July 2012, the AOJ did not address the claim for service connection for PTSD until 2015. On January 5, 2015, the AOJ issued a rating decision on the PTSD claim granting service connection for PTSD at a 100 percent disability rating, in response to a Board decision finding the Veteran's character of discharge was not a bar to VA benefits. See January 2014 Board decision. 

In general, if a veteran does not appeal a VA decision, that decision becomes final. See Cook v. Principi, 318 F.3d 1334, 1336 (Fed. Cir. 2002) (en banc). However, the VA must notify a veteran of his or her right to appeal the decision. 38 C.F.R. § 3.103(b)(1) (2004). Further, the VA must notify the veteran of the procedure to appeal, and the time limits within which he or she must appeal. Id. ("Such notice shall clearly set forth the decision made, any applicable effective date, the reason(s) for the decision, the right to a hearing on any issue involved in the claim, the right of representation and the right, as well as the necessary procedures and time limits, to initiate an appeal of the decision.").

If the VA fails to notify the veteran of this right, the claim remains open. 38 USCS §§ 7252(a), 7266 (2004); see also, Best v. Brown, 10 Vet. App. 322, 325 (1997) (finding that VA's failure to comply with notice requirements prevented a rating decision from becoming final). 

Here, the July 27, 2004 AOJ correspondence notified the Veteran of a decision that found he was not eligible for any VA benefits for his military service. It also notified the Veteran of the evidence the AOJ specifically considered. Further, it notified him that he may ask for a change in the character of his discharge, and/or apply for a correction, providing forms to do so. 

However, the July 27, 2004 AOJ correspondence did not notify the Veteran of his right to appeal the decision denying service connection for PTSD. It did not notify him of the time limits to appeal. Thus, the decision to deny service connection for PTSD did not become final. See, e.g., AG v. Peake, 536 F.3d 1306, 1308 (Fed. Cir. 2008) (finding the proceedings ongoing because of the VA's failure to notify the Veteran of his right to appeal). 

As the decision to deny the claim did not become final, the Veteran's claim remained open until the AOJ provided the proper notification on the PTSD claim. Here, the AOJ did not provide proper notice until issuing the January 2015 rating decision. See, e.g., AG v. Peake, 536 F.3d at 1310. 

Because the effective date of the award of service connection is based on the date that the application upon which service connection was eventually awarded was filed with the VA, the November 10, 2003 date is warranted. See, e.g., Lalonde v. West, 12 Vet. App. 377, 382 (1999); Juarez v. Peake, 21 Vet. App. 537, 544 (2008) (finding the subsequent rating decision, which properly provided notice and an opportunity to appeal was the proper effective date.). Thus, an earlier effective date, of November 10, 2003, for service connection for PTSD is granted.

There is no basis to grant an effective date earlier than November 10, 2003. This is because November 10, 2003 was the first date on which the VA received correspondence regarding the Veteran's PTSD claim for service connection. There are no documents dated prior to this on the matter. 38 U.S.C. § 5110(a); 38 C.F.R. § 3.400(q), (r).

Finally, having found the Veteran was not properly notified of his right to appeal the July 27, 2004 VA administrative decision, the Board finds it need not address the question of whether the July 24, 2006 VA treatment report should have been construed as an informal claim for benefits under the regulations in effect at the time.

 

 

Leetra J. Harris

Veterans Law Judge

Board of Veterans' Appeals

Attorney for the Board	Black, Julie A.

The Board's decision in this case is binding only with respect to the instant matter decided. This decision is not precedential and does not establish VA policies or interpretations of general applicability. 38 C.F.R. § 20.1303.
